subject: Queued response backlog affecting Arbor Health — status page notification & next steps
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Morris <lmorris@arborhealth.com>, ops@arborhealth.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Queued responses observed on your account — we're investigating

Hi Lena / Arbor ops team —

Quick heads up: starting at ~08:52 PST we observed a sustained increase in queued responses and elevated p95/p99 latency for requests routed from Arbor Health (tenant ID HB-83421). Impact was scoped to hosted inference in us-west via your standard model route.

What we're seeing now:
- p95 increased to ~1.8s (baseline ~0.6s) and p99 to ~4.3s for generation endpoints between 08:52–09:30 PST.
- Elevated request queueing correlated with a burst of prefix cache misses for a small subset of long-session traffic.

Immediate actions taken:
- Activated per-tenant fallback to warmed variant (v2-q8) for affected routes to reduce KV cache pressure.
- Temporarily increased concurrency cap for Arbor tenant while we validate stability.
- Opened an incident on our public status page (link below) and began full tracing capture.

Status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/RWI-2028-03-09-queued-backlog
Attachment: incident-timeline.pdf (short timeline and correlated metrics snapshot)

We’ll follow up with a short remediation note and a schedule for a postmortem within the week. For now: we expect service impact to be limited to increased latency and intermittent queued responses; request routing and model outputs are intact.

Apologies for the disruption — I’ll update as we have more.

Thanks,
Dylan

FYI / quick technical summary for the thread and for Arbor:

What we traced:
- Root correlation appears to be an intermittent prefix-cache invalidation on the prefetch layer; a small subset of long-lived sessions emitted heavy, varied prefixes which triggered miss storms across a handful of replicas around 08:50–08:55 PST. Miss storms multiplied RPCs and increased per-request planning latency.

Mitigation steps performed (completed by 09:40 PST):
1) Forced tenant-level routing to warmed model variant v2-q8 (reduces cache pressure).
2) Bypassed prefetch fanout for Arbor for 30 minutes to reduce simultaneous KV lookups.
3) Raised concurrency throttle for HB-83421 to allow backlog drain while monitoring CPU/GPU headroom.

Result: throughput returned to baseline and p99 dropped back toward expected ranges by ~09:40 PST. We continued validation and kept fallback active until we confirmed stable tail latency.

Next actions / follow-up:
- We will produce a short remediation note and a timeline (attached: mitigation-steps.txt).
- Security will run a focused audit on any captured logs (no evidence so far of payloads stored outside of normal telemetry).
- Postmortem scheduled; we'll invite Arbor SREs to participate.

Apologies again for the interruption — we’ll dig in and include long-term fixes (prefetch backoff, improved replica backpressure).

— Marissa

Subject: Incident RWI-2028-03-09 — status update and next steps

Hi Lena / Arbor team —

Thanks for your patience. Official update: we’ve declared the incident (RWI-2028-03-09) as "identified and mitigated" on the public status page. Full timeline and initial remediation steps are attached and linked below.

What changed since the last note:
- We confirmed steady throughput after the fallback; final validation completed at 10:05 PST and we marked the issue mitigated at 10:12 PST.
- No evidence at this time that customer payloads were exfiltrated or stored outside normal telemetry pipelines. Security will provide an audit artifact once they complete their review.

Status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/RWI-2028-03-09-queued-backlog
Postmortem invite: provisional postmortem scheduled for Mon, 12 Mar 2028, 10:00 AM PST — calendar invite to follow.

We’ll follow up with a short remediation plan and permanent fix timeline (prefetch backoff and replica-level backpressure improvements). If Arbor would like a dedicated postmortem slot, we can prioritize.

Sean Gallagher
Head of Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
